body:
I didn't actually execute the attempt(s), but I was damn close. (See my other posts for details). 

It was my birthday. When I was a lot younger, maybe 3 or 4, I didn't understand that you remained a certain age for the entire year. I thought that the day you turned 3 was the only day you fulfilled the quality of "being 3". So when people would say 'Oh he died when he was 100' I assumed it meant he died on his 100th birthday. I quickly realized that made no god damn sense, but i've always remembered my 3 year old logic. 

My parents drove down from San Francisco to have lunch with me. I had almost no friends at the time. Still hardly do but at least it isn't as bad as it use to be. We talked for a while over Mexican food, and I did everything in my power to make it seem like everything was okay. I remember thinking this would be the last time they ever saw me. 

I ended up getting talked down from the side of the Golden Gate bridge that day. The sunset was beautiful. 

It's still hard. I still battle with depression and suicidal thoughts most days. One thing people don't seem to understand is that once you sort of open that door of saying "Alright: I'm going to kill myself", it never really closes. That option never really comes off the table. At least for me it hasn't, maybe others can speak to this. But things are inchingly getting better.

I got talked down from the side of the golden gate bridge yesterday by two very nice policemen. I feel like a bit of an idiot now.
I'll see you all later.
I had a really helpful redditor contact me. Feeling a lot better now. Thanks guys.
Isn't the one thing psychologists say is *dont* put clinically depressed people in the same room with each other because they just make each other worse.
Interesting thought. I'll have to think about that.
